subject: Post-call recap: SLO drive, GPU tradeoffs & test plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Melanie Cho <melanie.cho@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: SLO drive, GPU tradeoffs & test plan

Melanie / Acme team — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps for dedicated performance validation.

Key SLOs you reiterated on the call:
- Streaming (incremental token delivery): customer-observed p95 latency <= 180ms for 512-token streams (incl. network and application glue).
- Non-streaming / batch generation: p99 latency <= 400ms for 512 tokens when routed to dedicated stack.
- Sustained throughput: baseline reserved throughput to support 800 QPS steady-state, with burst capacity to 2000 QPS during peak windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency target ~450 active sessions; planning tests up to 600 concurrent streams to validate headroom.

High-level GPU tradeoffs we discussed (summary):
- H100 (80GB): best single-request latency and largest batch headroom — yields lowest p95 at high concurrency for long-context / streaming workloads. Higher unit cost but fewer nodes.
- A100 (40GB): cost-effective for moderate sequence lengths and good for sharded or multi-instance deployments; may need more replicas to hit the same headroom as H100.
- L40S / L4-class: lower cost option with good throughput for short-context and high qps scenarios, but tail latency for long streaming context is higher and memory limits affect large KV caches.

Proposed validation test plan (48–72h window):
1) Baseline tests (smoke): verify end-to-end correctness and stable connections.
2) Config sweep A — H100 cluster test: 3 node config (H100 x3) with continuous batching, concurrency sweep 50 -> 600, measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming tokens and GPU util / memory.
3) Config sweep B — A100 cluster test: 5 node config (A100 x5), identical workload, track throughput per GPU and model sharding overhead.
4) Config sweep C — L40S cluster test: 8 node config (L40S x8) to validate cost/throughput tradeoffs for short-context heavy traffic.
5) Failure/resilience: simulate one-node failures and observe automatic fallback to model variants and queueing behavior.
6) KV cache effect: run with cold and warm cache to measure prefix-reuse benefits for your most common prompt sets.

Deliverables we'll produce after the window:
- CSV of raw perf samples (attached: gpu-benchmark-20270429.csv).
- Consolidated spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99, QPS, tokens/sec, GPU utilization (attached: acme-perf-targets.xlsx).
- Test plan + runbook for your ops team (attached: redwood-testplan-acme.md).

Action items / asks from you before we start:
- Provide a 48-72h test window (preferred: Mon-Wed next week).
- Shared API key / test account and a short allowlist range for source IPs (we can use a temporary token and restrict to Redwood test workers).
- A representative sample of prompts (10–20) and an SLO acceptance checklist — we used the ones on the call but attach anything further.
- Confirmation that Acme can accept a temporary monitoring link for the duration of the run (Grafana dashboard).

Costs & proposal (high-level):
- We'll provision a dedicated pool for the run. After validation we'll produce recommended reserved capacity profiles (nodes / vGPU mix) for a production commit.

Next step: if agreeable, we’ll schedule the validation window and I’ll loop in Eng (Aditya) to own the runbook and monitoring.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: gpu-benchmark-20270429.csv (csv, 1.1MB)]

From: Melanie Cho <melanie.cho@acmecloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-eng@acmecloud.com, sales@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO drive, GPU tradeoffs & test plan

Thanks Marcus — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we lock the window:

1) Data residency / logs: during the run, will logs / traces be stored in Redwood's hosted observability or pushed to our VPC? We prefer copies to be forwarded to our Splunk instance.
2) KV cache semantics: if we warm a session-heavy prefix, how quickly does cache eviction happen under high concurrency? We want to understand tail behavior for repeated sessions.
3) Concurrency cap: can Redwood enforce a per-customer concurrency cap on the dedicated pool to prevent noisy neighbors during the test?
4) Procurement: our procurement team would like a short write-up of the expected monthly reserve sizes and a representative price delta between H100 and A100-based pools for a pilot month.

We can do the test window next Tue-Wed (May 4–5) but procurement needs the pricing note to sign off.

— Melanie
Melanie Cho | CTO, AcmeCloud

On Fri, Apr 30, 2027 at 09:15 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Melanie / Acme team — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps for dedicated performance validation...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Melanie Cho <melanie.cho@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO drive, GPU tradeoffs & test plan

Melanie — answers inline and a small update to the test plan.

1) Logs / traces: we can stream traces and metrics to your Splunk/S3 endpoint for the run. Aditya will coordinate the forwarder; we need your Splunk ingest token and an allowlist IP.

2) KV cache semantics: eviction is LRU by segment; in our lab runs you typically see meaningful degradation after sustained 2–3x the working set capacity. For the validation we'll run a cold->warm cycle and report exact evict rates; one mitigation is an LRU pin for hot prefixes (we can enable that during the pilot).

3) Concurrency cap: yes — we can enforce a soft cap and queue or slow-start additional sessions. We'll propose a per-customer concurrency ceiling for the dedicated pool and a policy to prioritize your traffic during peaks.

4) Pricing note for procurement: see quick estimate below (pilot month):
- H100-backed reserved pool (3x nodes): est. $XX,XXX / month (higher unit cost, fewer nodes).
- A100-backed reserved pool (5x nodes): est. $YY,YYY / month (mid cost, more replicas).
- L40S-backed pool (8x nodes): est. $ZZ,ZZZ / month (lowest per-node cost but more nodes).

I’ll have finance produce a formal quote but wanted to give procurement the ballpark to unblock scheduling.

Test plan tweak: add a short 4 hour mixed-traffic run (short-context burst + long-context streaming) to understand mixed workload interference.

If Tue-Wed (May 4–5) works we’ll reserve engineers and monitoring. Please send the Splunk token & prompt set by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Marcus

Adding a quick note from the ops/runbook side: during the streaming p95 measurements we will capture both the Redwood-observed service latency and end-to-end latency (client -> Redwood -> client) so you have visibility into network overhead. We’ll provide a Grafana link with the following panels: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, QPS, GPU util, mem used, cache hit rate, and queue depth.

Dashboard (read-only) will be shared at the start of the window: https://redwood-internal/grafana/d/abc/perf-acme

Also: we'll flag any test where p95 exceeds target for longer than 5 minutes and automatically pause the run for triage.

— Lauren
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
